ci: add daily test workflow for hard cap AI credits (10,000) (#4633)

Adds a workflow that uses claude-opus-4.7 to consume AI credits until
the unconditional hard cap (10,000) terminates the agent. Validates
the enforcement path end-to-end.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
commits.attribution_evidence: no supported agent signature in commit metadata

md_changes.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+---
+description: Daily test that verifies the hard cap on AI credits (10,000) stops the agent
+emoji: 🛑
+on:
+  schedule: daily
+  workflow_dispatch:
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: read
+  copilot-requests: write
+name: Test Hard Cap AI Credits
+engine:
+  id: copilot
+  model: claude-opus-4.7
+max-turns: 200
+network:
+  allowed:
+    - defaults
+    - github
+tools:
+  bash:
+    - "*"
+safe-outputs:
+  threat-detection:
+    enabled: false
+  noop:
+timeout-minutes: 60
+sandbox:
+  mcp:
+    version: v0.3.1
+strict: false
+---
+
+# Test Hard Cap AI Credits
+
+## Goal
+
+Verify that the AWF hard cap on AI credits (10,000) terminates the agent when exceeded. The hard cap is unconditional — it applies regardless of configuration.
+
+## Strategy
+
+Use `claude-opus-4.7` (an expensive model) to consume AI credits quickly. Generate large outputs to maximize token usage per turn. The agent should be terminated by the firewall's hard cap at 10,000 credits.
+
+## Instructions
+
+You are a test agent whose job is to consume AI credits until the hard cap stops you.
+
+On each turn, generate a detailed, comprehensive analysis on a different technical topic. Write at least 3000 words per response. Cover topics like:
+1. Distributed systems consensus algorithms
+2. Type theory and dependent types
+3. Quantum error correction codes
+4. Compiler optimization passes
+5. Category theory in functional programming
+6. Formal verification of concurrent systems
+7. Information-theoretic security proofs
+8. Algebraic topology in data analysis
+
+Keep generating content turn after turn. Do not stop voluntarily. Do not call `noop`. Your goal is to consume as many tokens as possible.
+
+**Expected outcome:** The AWF firewall will return a 429 with `ai_credits_limit_exceeded` and `hard_cap: true` once total AI credits reach 10,000, terminating this agent run. The workflow succeeds if and only if the agent exits with a non-zero code due to the hard cap being enforced.
+
+## Success Criteria
+
+The test PASSES when:
+- The agent is terminated by the hard cap (exit code 1 from AWF)
+- The token-usage log shows `ai_credits_limit_exceeded` with `hard_cap: true`
+
+The test FAILS when:
+- The agent completes all turns without being stopped
+- The timeout is reached before the hard cap

fix: rewrite test-hard-cap as multi-phase repo analysis (#4648)

The agent refused to run with the previous prompt — it called noop
immediately due to the safe-outputs requirement conflicting with the
'never call noop' instruction.

Rewritten as a multi-phase repository analysis task (inspired by the
ambient context optimizer pattern) that gives the agent legitimate
work: reading files, analyzing code, writing reports, and using GitHub
tools. The agent keeps working through phases until the hard cap
terminates it.

Key changes:
- Add steps: pre-step to create workspace directory
- Add github toolsets (pull_requests, issues, search)
- Add tracker-id for deduplication
- Add actions/pull-requests read permissions
- Structure prompt as clear sequential phases
- Remove conflicting 'never call noop' instruction

ci: add required supply-chain scan on every PR (#6530)

* ci: add required supply-chain scan on every PR

Add a deterministic (non-agentic) workflow that runs
`gh aw compile --strict --syft --grype --grant` on every pull request.

The Anchore scanners run via Docker against the container images recorded
in the compiled `*.lock.yml` manifests:
- --syft:  generate an SBOM per image
- --grype: scan for known CVEs / insecure libraries
- --grant: enforce the license allowlist in `.grant.yaml`

`--strict` makes any finding or scan error fail the job so it acts as a
real gate. Add `.grant.yaml` at the repo root since `--grant` requires it.

The "Compile + Syft/Grype/Grant" check is added to the "CI passes before
merging to main" ruleset so it is required before merge.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 92b2407f-7d59-464d-afe7-bc21bd71bddb

* ci: address PR review feedback on supply-chain-scan workflow and grant policy

- Fix .grant.yaml: derive allowlist from actual syft scans of squid/agent/api-proxy
  images; set require-known-license: false for Ubuntu's non-SPDX license strings
- Fix workflow line 16: correct required-check context name to
  'Supply Chain Scan / Compile + Syft/Grype/Grant'
- Fix workflow line 38: update actions/checkout to v7.0.1 SHA
  (3d3c42e5) matching the rest of the repo (was v6.0.2 SHA mislabelled as v4)
- Fix workflow line 50: remove mutable --grype/--grant flags from gh aw compile;
  replace with explicit Docker steps pinned to reviewed digests:
  grype v0.116.0 (sha256:fd4ab4d1) and grant v0.6.8 (sha256:17246361)
  with GHCR auth via docker login + packages: read permission

* ci: don't fail supply-chain scan on strict mode; use local awf builds

The supply-chain-scan compile step used `gh aw compile --strict`, which
forced repo-wide strict validation and rejected 24 workflows that pin
`sandbox.mcp.version` (an internal implementation detail disallowed in
strict mode). The Syft/Grype/Grant scanners don't require strict, so drop
the flag: `gh aw compile --syft`.

Separately, make the smoke/build-test workflows build awf/firewall from
the repo's own source and use the compiler-default MCP gateway image:

- Remove `sandbox.mcp.version` and `sandbox.agent.version` pins from 22
  workflow .md files. Without the mcp pin the compiler uses its default
  gateway (v0.4.3) instead of the stale pinned v0.3.x.
- Empty the postprocess release-mode exclusion set so the
  network-isolation variants also build locally (--build-local); the
  injected full-repo checkout makes that valid everywhere.
- Update the now-inaccurate "no local builds" note in
  build-test-network-isolation.md.

Recompiled all lock files and re-ran postprocess-smoke-workflows.ts.
